text:
Meera: Heads-up — noticed a sudden p99 spike for the /v2/generate route starting ~1758888800. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/routes/v2/generate/kpis
Alex: I can see it in the per-route card. p50 ~12ms, p95 ~120ms, p99 jumped to ~420ms. Throughput stable ~70 rps. Error rate ticked to 0.8%.
Jordan: Any correlation with kernel routing changes or a new rollout? saw a canary yesterday that toggled kernel-selection-policy.
Meera: Yes, we rolled the new kernel selector (hash 3a7b9c) 3h ago. Also noticed KV cache hit rate dropped from ~96% to ~40% around the same time.
Lina: if KV hit rate dropped that would explain tails — prefix cache helps reduce token generation work. Do we have token-level waterfall traces for affected requests?
Meera: Uploaded a sample trace to the perf bucket: gs://perf-traces/1758889/trace-3a7b9c.json
Dan: I pulled a flamegraph — looks like lots of time in attention_kv::restore and kernel_fallback path. Kernel selection appears to choose a quantized kernel that falls back to a slow reference for certain sequence lengths.
Alex: That matches my local repro — for sequences >=512 the selector picks int8-fast but we hit a fallback to scalar-emi which is ~4-5x slower.
Jordan: Is our batching heuristic increasing batch sizes under that route? Larger batches + fallback kernel would produce higher p99 even if p50 unaffected.
Meera: Checking batching histograms on the route card: median batch size 2, but tail 64+ for some bursts. Batching policy 'aggressive' seems to be in effect for this customer group.
Lina: Could be two factors: (1) kernel selection table missing a sequence-length entry -> fallback, (2) KV cache invalidation spike causing more recomputation. Both amplify tail.
perf-bot: Alert: route /v2/generate p99 > 400ms for 12m. Investigations: KV-cache-hit-rate down 56pp, kernel-fallback-rate up 18pp.
Dan: I instrumented kernel selector to emit chosen_kernel and fallback boolean. Quick patch:

```json
# instrumentation config snippet
emit: ["chosen_kernel", "fallback", "seq_len", "batch_size"]
sampler: 0.01
```

Pushing now as PR 4821.
Alex: Nice. Also adding token-level breakdown to the Console card (prefix-restore | kernel-run | batching-queue | postproc). That should make it easier for product owners to see what dominates the tail.
Meera: For immediate mitigation can we force kernel routing to prefer fp16 path for seq_len>=512? Temporary knob 'kernel.force_fp16_on_tail=true'
Jordan: We can hotflip that via rollout-control. I'll create a canary for 5% traffic to verify p99 drops.
Lina: Also setting KV warmup policy to avoid broad invalidation during that window. Dan, do you have a query to find requests that caused large KV churn?
Dan: Yup, I'll run it and annotate the route insights with an example query. Rough query: SELECT req_id, seq_len, batch_size, kv_hit FROM route_events WHERE ts BETWEEN 1758888600 AND 1758889200 AND route='/v2/generate' LIMIT 50
Meera: After enabling the fp16 force on 5% canary, p99 on that slice dropped from ~420ms to ~130ms in 10m. Can we roll to 50% and monitor.
Alex: Putting a per-route KPI slice in Console: slice: "kv-low & seq>=512" showing p50/p95/p99 + sample traces. Also will add a small note in the UX: "Investigate kernel fallback or KV churn" with a one-click drilldown.
Jordan: After widening canary to 50% p99 global fell to ~160ms, KV hit rate stabilized to ~90% after we reverted the cache invalidation job.
Meera: Postmortem items: (1) Add unit test for kernel selector coverage across seq_len buckets, (2) Add alert for sudden KV hit-rate drops on a per-route basis, (3) Instrumentation: token-level waterfall must be visible in the route card within 10s of request capture.
Lina: I'll own the KV alert. Suggest threshold: drop >15 percentage points in 5m for any route with >20 rps.
Dan: I'll merge PR 4821 for selector emissions and update the telemetry schema. Need to coordinate with product for Console UX additions.
Alex: Creating a short runbook note in the Console route card: steps to toggle kernel.force_fp16_on_tail and to check KV warmup. @oncall please follow if this resurfaces.
perf-bot: Note: next auto-check scheduled in 5m.
Meera: Thanks all. Filed follow-ups: ENG-3581 (selector tests), ENG-3582 (console waterfall UI), ENG-3583 (kv alerts). Closing thread once PRs are merged.
Alex: Thanks — nice cross-team quick loop. :thumbsup:
